summary.note: Keyed by manifest object name. "theorems" lists what constrains the part and the audit verdict of each; "how" says in what way; "notConstrained" lists what no theorem touches. Organs are grounded only structurally through the blueprint certificate where their ontology id is a node of it. Nothing here says the model is correct; it says which parts a machine-checked statement reaches.

skin_L.label: skin and scales, left half
skin_L.blueprint: present in the certified blueprint (term is a node of the well-formed graph)
skin_L.how: Skin: under isometry its area scales as L² (areaLaw_ratio), which says nothing about the fish beyond the hypothesis; the body planform area (A3 in Park and Choi, 0.004474 m² for L3) is part of the lifting area in vmin_le. Scale pattern is a procedural texture, not data.

pectoral_fin_L.label: pectoral fin (membrane), left; enlarged, spread for gliding
pectoral_fin_L.geometry_basis: evidence: pectoral fin length / standard length = 0.687 (median of 49 flying-fish specimens, Daane et al. 2021 Curr Biol Data S1A, recomputed in genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json); fin shape, spread and ray layout schematic
pectoral_fin_L.blueprint: present in the certified blueprint (term is a node of the well-formed graph)
pectoral_fin_L.how: Wing size: vmin_le bounds the lifting area from below for a given mass and speed, S ≥ 2W/(ρ v² C_L,max). For specimen L3 (W = 0.588 N, C_L,max = 0.78, ρ = 1.225) the area needed is 0.012316 m² at 10 m/s and 0.003079 m² at 20 m/s; the measured lifting area (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) is 0.012688 m², so at the low end of the field speeds the fins are about as large as the bound requires and at 20 m/s four times larger. areaLaw_ratio and wingLoading_ratio say how S and W/S would scale under isometry; Davenport 1992 measures 1.834 and 1.236 instead, so isometry fails within E. obtusirostris. vmin_ratio and powerRequired_ratio give the √L and L^3.5 scalings under the named hypotheses; not evaluated (one size class). The fin LENGTH ratio 0.687 (Daane 2021) is an input the model carries; no theorem constrains fin length as such, nor aspect ratio or fin shape.
notConstrained: fin length as a fraction of standard length (0.687 is an input, not a theorem)
aspect ratio (9.0-10.7, Park and Choi) and its effect on L/D
the four-wing (pelvic) contribution beyond its area

pectoral_fin_ray_L_01.label: pectoral fin ray 1 (lepidotrichium), left
pectoral_fin_ray_L_01.geometry_basis: ray length follows the pectoral fin length ratio (evidence, longest ray); ray count 14 is illustrative
pectoral_fin_ray_L_01.blueprint: ontology term not in the certified blueprint
pectoral_fin_ray_L_01.how: Fin rays as slender beams (R9): under the aerodynamic load on a fin, which scales with fin area at fixed speed and C_L, the load is sheet-like, so bendingStress_ratio_sheet applies and predicts size-independent ray stress under similar sections, with no size limit; under a body-like load (R9a) stress ∝ L and a limit follows. Which applies is the empirical fork; inputs (ray section modulus, σ_max) are missing, so nothing is evaluated.

caudal_fin.label: caudal fin (membrane), forked, lower lobe longer
caudal_fin.blueprint: no ontology id on this piece
caudal_fin.how: Caudal fin (the propulsor for taxiing and launch): no theorem constrains its shape or the longer lower lobe; froude_ratio constrains only how the swimming speed it produces scales across sizes at equal Froude number, and the launch speed is measured for one size class only (Makiguchi 2013, 3.87-5.15 m/s, estimated).

caudal_fin_rays.label: caudal fin rays (19, illustrative)
caudal_fin_rays.blueprint: no ontology id on this piece
caudal_fin_rays.how: Caudal fin rays as beams under the taxiing load (R9): no data; which load family applies is not known.

muscle_L.label: trunk musculature: myomeres (W-shaped segments), left
muscle_L.blueprint: no ontology id on this piece
muscle_L.how: Trunk musculature: the only theorems touching it carry Thompson's muscle premise (power available = f p M) as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS; they prove P_avail ∝ L³ under it and the existence of a size limit for powered flight. f and p are unmeasured for Exocoetidae, and a gliding fish does not fly under muscle power, so these constrain the launch and taxiing phase at most. No theorem proves anything about muscle itself.
